errorsLogged:
The final run wrote 21 JSON files to /mnt/project-files/playbox-2/evidence/journey, one per launch test, named by the test-title slug. journey.spec.ts does not use the fixture, so it has none. Every file has status passed and summary.assertedUnexpected 0. There were 0 unexpected entries of any kind: console, pageerror, requestfailed or response.

Expected entries, each with the reason the test declared:
- New GB member: 2 responses (451 POST /api/generations, 451 POST /api/uploads) and the 2 matching console "Failed to load resource ... 451" lines.
- Scanner match: 403 POST /api/uploads and 401 POST /api/auth/login, plus their 2 console lines.
- Chargeback: 403 POST /api/checkout plus its console line.
- Service-worker offline test: 2 console lines (net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED for an RSC prefetch, and Next's "Failed to fetch RSC payload ... Falling back to browser navigation").
- Every page-driven test: 4 to 84 requestfailed net::ERR_ABORTED entries, labelled expected by the helper's built-in allowance (the browser cancelling prefetches or preloads on navigation). The service-worker test also has the declared net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED for the offline /collection navigation.
- The manifest and sw.js tests open no page, so their logs are empty.

API calls made through request contexts are asserted directly in the tests and are not page events: the webhook 400s and the /api/media 403s.

In an earlier run of the same spec, the JSON for "after verification previews load…" recorded an unexpected pageerror, "Minified React error #418", on /collection, and the fixture failed the test. That led to the hydration fix.

appBugs.summary: Text computed from the clock (relativeTime 'Xm ago', elapsed 'Ns', admin 'open Xh') and the device locale (toLocaleDateString) in server-rendered client components broke hydration (React #418) whenever server and device times differed: a second or minute boundary during hydration, or any device clock skew. React then discarded the server HTML.
appBugs.evidence:
An earlier launch run failed. The evidence JSON for 'after verification previews load…' has pageerror 'Minified React error #418; ...args[]=text' on /collection while the Library was being reloaded.

Deterministic repro (scratchpad probe-clock-check.cjs, browser clock 10 minutes ahead): server HTML said '5m ago', the client rendered '15m ago', and #418 fired.

After the fix: the same probe at 10 minutes ahead reported 0 page errors on /collection, /collection/<id>, /studio, /settings, /pricing, /projects, /train and /, with the server text kept. The final suite also logged 0 page errors.

The fix adds suppressHydrationWarning to 22 elements in 11 client components. Nothing else changes.

appBugs.summary: Every not-found page answers HTTP 200 instead of 404. The route loading skeletons from 64e1a48 (src/app/loading.tsx, collection/loading.tsx, collection/[id]/loading.tsx and the other [id] routes) wrap async pages in Suspense, so Next.js sends the shell with 200 before notFound() runs. The 404 UI ('A loose thread') and a noindex meta then stream in. The other member still sees none of the content; only the status code is wrong.
appBugs.evidence:
The first full run failed journey.spec.ts:93 with 'Expected: 404 Received: 200'; the page snapshot showed the 404 UI.

curl as a signed-in member returned 200 plus name="robots" content="noindex" for /collection/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000, /collection/not-a-uuid, /templates/no-such-template-xyz, /creators/no-such-creator and /projects/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000.

It is not a small local fix: it needs those loading boundaries removed from routes that can 404, or existence decided before the boundary. So the journey test is test.fixme with its assertions unchanged.

variantsChosen: Upload path: through the real create-panel UI (Image to image radio, setInputFiles on the upload-input testid, then the 'Before you upload' consent sheet), not page.request. This exercises the consent flow and the alert the user actually sees, for the GB 451, the scanner's 403 and the clean 201.

Replay check: both variants. (1) Deliveries the test cannot sign validly (no signature, a forged v1, a correct signature 10 minutes old) must each return 400 with codes unsigned, bad_signature and replayed, and leave the balance unchanged. (2) The test signs a sale event with the documented dev-only sandbox constant from src/server/payments/providers/sandbox.ts and posts the identical body and header twice: the first returns processed and the second duplicate, credits are granted once and one history row appears. Why: the signed body the app builds server-side in /api/pricing/sandbox never reaches the browser, so a captured real delivery cannot be replayed.

Service-worker emulation: playwright.config.ts sets PW_EXPERIMENTAL_SERVICE_WORKER_NETWORK_EVENTS=1 so context.setOffline and the GB extraHTTPHeaders also apply to the worker's own fetches, as on a real device and edge. Without it Chromium's worker stayed online and the offline page never showed.

Private page offline check in a second tab: after a failed offline navigation, Chromium's emulated navigator.onLine flips back to true in new documents, and the offline page's online listener reloads the first tab. The check therefore reads a fresh tab right away. It accepts either the browser's ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED or the offline page, and asserts no balance and no Library.

Server start: scripts/e2e-serve.mjs replaces the cp-based webServer command. It copies .next/static and public/ next to server.js and finds server.js when Next nests the standalone output (this worktree sits inside another checkout that has a lockfile).

Evidence capture is on pages only. Calls made through APIRequestContext (webhook posts, /api/media probes) are asserted directly in the tests. journey.spec.ts was not wrapped with the evidence fixture; that was optional, and its only change is the fixme.
notCovered: The journey test 'another member cannot see that creation or its media' is fixme, so none of its assertions ran: the page 404, the API 404s for GET, derive and DELETE, the forged-media 403 and the cross-site POST 403.
Real push delivery and the push toggle with VAPID keys configured: the e2e stack has no keys, so only the 'not configured' state is covered.
The real install prompt (beforeinstallprompt) and an installed standalone launch: headless Chromium cannot show them. Only the manifest, icons, worker and Settings card are checked.
A validly signed media URL for the matched asset: the signing secret is random per run and the admin page exposes no URL. Only unsigned and forged requests are shown to be refused (403).
Real payment processors and real age-verification providers: the suite covers the labelled sandboxes only.

The pwa-02 screenshot is blank: headless Chromium renders its own network-error page blank. The test's evidence is the asserted navigation error (ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED), plus no balance and no Library heading.
The hydration fix was verified with a clock-skew probe outside the suite (scratchpad probe-418-clock.cjs and probe-clock-check.cjs). No committed e2e test runs with a skewed browser clock.
Admin pages with long-open or old takedowns, which would exercise the 24h 'open Xh' styling, were not loaded under clock skew.
